key_insight: The paper reformulates 2D Stokes flow on irregular domains as an unfitted boundary algebraic equation problem using lattice Green’s functions and Calderón preconditioning to obtain accurate, stable solutions without singular quadrature.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical high-order solver for complex fluid-structure or exterior-flow geometries on Cartesian grids, with strong conditioning and discrete incompressibility suitable for engineering simulations.
method: Builds velocity/pressure lattice Green’s functions from free-space Laplace LGFs on a staggered MAC grid.
Represents homogeneous fields using sources only on thin boundary layers and enforces Dirichlet data by local interpolation at cut points.
Uses sampled-normal rank updates and a discrete Calderón preconditioner with padded FFTs for fast volume convolutions and GMRES solve.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive validation on multiply connected domains, narrow gaps, and Moffatt eddies, achieving second-order velocity/pressure convergence, solver-accurate discrete divergence, and orders-of-magnitude condition-number reduction.
watch_item: The Calderón preconditioner remains more demanding in narrow-gap and fine-grid interior cases, so robustness and cost may degrade for very challenging geometries.
paper_title: An unfitted boundary algebraic equation method with Calderón preconditioning for 2D Stokes flow in irregular geometry
